readerQuestion: How do I configure Home Assistant Adaptive Lighting so an existing lamp follows the day without overriding reading presets or behaving unexpectedly at bedtime?
directAnswer: Install the community Adaptive Lighting integration, configure one existing dimmable tunable-white lamp, keep manual takeover and explicit-value turn-on protection enabled, and test manual hold/resume before expanding. Sleep mode needs its own on/off policy; v1.32.0 sleep-reset settings must be changed if bedtime should preserve a manual hold. The light integration still determines local/cloud control.
originalContribution: Sections 3-5 provide a bounded reading-lamp profile (20-70% daily brightness, 2700-4000 K, 10%/2700 K sleep settings), a five-step household acceptance test, and a two-action resume script. The troubleshooting table maps outcomes to the next reversible check. The configuration assumes a supporting lamp; the numbers are example preferences, not measurements. Release-code review showed manual-control reset already reapplies to on lights, so the final script avoids a redundant apply command.
limitations: Documentation and released-code research only; no physical bulb, Home Assistant runtime, latency, illumination, or cloud-outage test. YAML parsed and field names checked against v1.32.0 service definitions, which does not establish runtime or hardware compatibility. Device states, fades and external-control reporting can vary. Custom-integration settings are version dependent. Cover is an AI-generated editorial room illustration, not an installed or tested product.
proofreadFixes: Added explicit pause_all behavior so a brightness hold also preserves color; explained the counterintuitive take_over_control name; scoped reset_manual_control_on_sleep_mode_change to v1.32.0 and changed the example to false so sleep mode does not clear the reading hold. Kept detect_non_ha_changes off and stated that vendor-app/direct-remote changes may be missed. Removed the unnecessary adaptive_lighting.apply call after verifying that manual_control=false already reapplies settings to reported-on lights. Added the reported-state caveat and shared-profile warning. Defined kelvin and stated example brightness is a command, not a light-output measurement. Added a sideways-scroll hint and keyboard focus for the YAML block. The visible method note initially lacked the publish gate’s research-method class; corrected it without hiding the disclosure. Verified all new metadata, including Twitter, matches this article and September 27 date. Final automated grandma proofreading: PASS; no human or expert review claimed. Final mobile inspection found a wide explanation column required panning within a single cell; changed both tables to fixed equal-width columns so each cell fits inside the mobile scroll viewport.

claimChecks.claim: Adaptive Lighting is community custom software; installing its files through HACS is separate from adding/configuring it in Home Assistant.
Adaptive Lighting v1.32.0 requires Home Assistant 2025.9 or newer and supplies the option to preserve manual control across sleep-mode changes.
The UI configuration route selects the lights and creates the main, brightness, color and sleep switches; a duplicate YAML profile is not required.
The example is contingent on working brightness and color-temperature controls; on/off-only hardware cannot acquire those capabilities through an automation.

only_once=false enables continued adaptation. The documented defaults are interval 90 seconds and transition 45 seconds; the four-minute check is an allowance for multiple updates, not a measured performance claim.

take_over_control allows manual takeover; pause_all pauses both attributes; explicit brightness/color on commands are respected with adapt_only_on_bare_turn_on. External changes need separate verification.
Sleep mode remains active until switched off, is restored across restart and does not automatically clear at sunrise.

Released v1.32.0 handle_set_manual_control_service resets the mark and immediately updates when the profile is on; _update_attrs_and_maybe_adapt_lights filters to reported-on lights. The final two-action resume script therefore does not need a separate apply and does not request lights reported off to turn on. Incorrect state reporting remains a stated caveat.
The resume script data keys entity_id, lights and manual_control match the released service definition. Its YAML was parsed locally, not executed on hardware.
A one-shot apply and a manual-control reset serve different purposes; ongoing adjustment also depends on the enabled profile and adaptation settings.

State-reporting errors and unsupported transitions can cause unexpected bulb behavior; the first diagnostic is a reversible one-lamp check with adaptation off, without factory resets or critical lighting interruptions.

incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: A reader whose saved scene is overwritten may want a continuously adapting alternative with explicit manual holds; link only after explaining which routine owns the light.

incomingLinkOpportunities.section: Other practical questions — Does it change the color of the light?
incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: The existing example changes brightness during a morning ramp. Readers asking about white-tone changes throughout the day can follow this separate custom-integration setup, with a caution to avoid competing control of the same lamp.
